newsitem.title: UK: Weak silver steers London precious metals lower.
newsitem.headline: Weak silver steers London precious metals lower.

text.p: A bout of fund selling of silver in New York kept precious metals under pressure in Europe on Friday but traders cited underlying support.
Gold fixed at $348.35 per ounce versus $348.75 on Wednesday and against a close of $348.40/$348.90, but traders said activity was slim and prices were steered by silver movements.
"I think people are unsure which way to jump and are happy to keep a low profile before the weekend," said one dealer.
Gold had held well so far, he said, but if silver probed further into lower levels on disenchanted fund selling, it could break down through support, currently pegged at $345.00.
"Gold's direction is probably dependant on silver. If silver recovers this afternoon up to $4.80-$4.85, gold will hold its $347.00-$352.00 range," the dealer said.
"But if silver comes under pressure I'm not quite sure if there will be as much support as there has been over the last few days," he added.
Meanwhile silver was digesting its fresh overnight losses which carried it to its lowest level since mid-January of $4.65 per ounce. But dealers said selling seemed to have abated.
"If anything there is sporadic buying around," said one, adding that nearby chart support came in at $4.65-$4.70.
Others saw critical support at $4.55/$4.60, which, if breached could send the market sharply lower. At 1030 GMT it was indicated at $4.74/$4.75 versus Thursday's close of $4.82/$4.84.
"It's very much in the hands of funds who are driving the market and they don't like to trade at any other time zone than New York," said one dealer.
"It does look overdone but that doesn't mean they (the funds) can't come and have another go," he said.
Dealers said tumbling U.S. stock markets due to fears of higher interest rates, could come into play in gold although the market has yet to see a cash influx from equities or bonds.
Some technical analysts said a break through $345.00 on bullion would signal a move down to $336.00.
Weak silver also drove platinum lower but dealers noted underlying support while there were no talks between Russia and Japan on PGM sale contracts which expired at the end of 1996.
Market analysts said although Japanese buyers were tapping Zurich for their immediate needs, a delay in talks for a few more weeks would unsettle the market.
Platinum was indicated at $363.50/$364.50, down $1.50 on the day, while palladium was $0.50 higher at $146.00/$147.00.
